title: Comparing, Ordering and Rounding Whole Numbers
seo_title: Grade 4 Comparing and Rounding Whole Numbers Worksheets (TEKS 4.2C, 4.2D, STAAR)
standard_text: 4.2C compare and order whole numbers to 1,000,000,000 and represent comparisons using the symbols >, <, or =; 4.2D round whole numbers to a given place value through the hundred thousands place
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 worksheets for Texas TEKS 4.2C and 4.2D: compare and order numbers to a billion, round to the nearest thousand, ten thousand and hundred thousand, and real-world problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Compare from the left. Round by looking at the digit to the right.
key_sub: The first place with different digits decides which number is greater. 5 or more rounds up.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A number with more digits is greater. With the same number of digits, compare from the left; the first place where the digits differ decides.
  • > means greater than, < means less than.
  • To round, look at the digit to the right of the rounding place: 5 or more rounds up, 4 or less rounds down. All places to the right become 0.

Examples

Example

Compare 4,302,118 and 4,320,118.

Same millions and hundred thousands.

Ten thousands: 0 < 2.

Answer: 4,302,118 < 4,320,118

Example

Round 6,748,215 to the nearest hundred thousand.

Hundred thousands digit: 7.

The next digit is 4, so round down.

Answer: 6,700,000

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Comparing the last digits firstStart from the greatest place.
Rounding to the wrong placeUnderline the rounding place before you look to its right.
Rounding 5 down5 or more rounds up.

faq.a: Compare and order whole numbers to 1,000,000,000 and represent comparisons using >, < or =.
Round whole numbers to a given place value through the hundred thousands place.

faq.q: How do you round to the nearest hundred thousand?
faq.a: Look at the ten thousands digit. If it is 5 or more, add 1 to the hundred thousands digit. Then write zeros in all the places to the right.
Rounded numbers are easier to understand and compare, like saying a city has about 2,300,000 people.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Line up the places and compare from the left. Both have the same digits until the tens place: 4 tens is more than 3 tens. So 25,843 > 25,834. 25,843 is the greatest.

items.q: Which number is the least?
items.e: Line up the places and compare from the left. Both have the same digits until the thousands place: 7 thousands is more than 2 thousands. So 12,789 < 17,829, and 12,789 is the least.

items.q: Which comparison is true?
items.e: Line up the places and compare from the left. Both have the same digits until the tens place: 7 tens is more than 3 tens. So 563,573 > 563,537.

items.q: Three baseball games had these crowds: 28,753 fans, 27,835 fans and 27,853 fans. Which list shows the numbers from least to greatest?
items.e: Compare from the left. 27,835 < 27,853, because in the tens place 3 < 5. 27,853 < 28,753, because in the thousands place 7 < 8. So the order is 27,835; 27,853; 28,753.

items.q: Round 499,999 to the nearest thousand.
items.e: Round to the nearest thousand: 499,999 is between 499,000 and 500,000. The digit to the right of the thousands place is 9, so round up. The thousands digit is 9, so adding 1 thousand regroups: 499,000 + 1,000 = 500,000. Answer: 500,000.

items.q: A park had 72,480 visitors this year. A sign says “about 72,000 visitors.” To which place was the number rounded?
items.e: 72,480 to the nearest thousand: the hundreds digit is 4, so round down to 72,000. To the nearest hundred it would be 72,500, and to the nearest ten thousand it would be 70,000.

items.q: A city has 284,516 people. What is its population rounded to the nearest ten thousand?
items.e: Round to the nearest ten thousand: 284,516 is between 280,000 and 290,000. The digit to the right of the ten thousands place is 4, so round down. Answer: 280,000.

items.q: What is the greatest whole number that rounds to 50,000 when you round to the nearest thousand?
items.e: Numbers from 49,500 to 50,499 round to 50,000. 50,500 has a 5 in the hundreds place, so it rounds up to 51,000.

items.q: A video has 349,612 views. Rounded to the nearest hundred thousand, about how many views is that?

items.q: A school district has 24,951 students. What is that number rounded to the nearest hundred?
items.e: Round to the nearest hundred: 24,951 is between 24,900 and 25,000. The digit to the right of the hundreds place is 5, so round up. The hundreds digit is 9, so adding 1 hundred regroups: 24,900 + 100 = 25,000. Answer: 25,000.

items.q: At a baseball game, 41,736 fans were in the stadium. A news report rounds this to the nearest thousand. What number does the report give?
items.e: Round to the nearest thousand: 41,736 is between 41,000 and 42,000. The digit to the right of the thousands place is 7, so round up. Answer: 42,000.

items.q: A concert sold about 30,000 tickets, rounded to the nearest ten thousand. Which could be the exact number of tickets sold?
items.e: Numbers from 25,000 to 34,999 round to 30,000. 25,104 is in that range. 35,200 and 38,000 round up to 40,000, and 24,870 rounds down to 20,000.
